chunks: And it was narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim that he said:

Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed by me while I was performing salat (prayer) upon al-Ṭabarī, and I had placed something over it. So he said: “What is the matter with you that you do not perform sajdah upon it? Is it not from the vegetation of the earth?”

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh said in his epistle: “Perform sajdah upon the earth or upon what the earth produces, and do not perform sajdah upon the Madinan mats, because their straps are made of leather.”

And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about gypsum over which dung and the bones of the dead are burned, then the mosque is plastered with it: may sajdah be performed upon it? So he wrote to him in his own handwriting: “Indeed, water and fire have purified it.”
And Dāwūd ibn Yazīd asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام about papers and sheets with writing on them: is sajdah upon them permissible? So he wrote: “It is permissible.”

key_terms.الْجِصِّ: gypsum or plaster discussed as a mosque surface for sajdah
key_terms.الْحُصُرِ الْمَدَنِيَّةِ: Madinan mats, here mentioned as unsuitable for sajdah due to their leather straps
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: filth or dung used in firing the gypsum
key_terms.الْقَرَاطِيسِ: papers or sheets upon which sajdah is asked about
key_terms.الْمَاءَ وَ النَّارَ: water and fire, mentioned as means by which the gypsum was purified
key_terms.نَبَاتِ الْأَرْضِ: that which grows from the earth and may serve as a valid surface for sajdah

ai.seo_question: What materials are permissible for sajdah in Shia Islam during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal rulings of sajdah regarding what may be used as its surface during salat (prayer). It affirms the permissibility of performing sajdah on what grows from the earth, addresses the impurity question concerning treated gypsum, and permits sajdah on written papers. The narration is significant in Shia fiqh for determining valid materials for prostration.
